papers.title: Alternative splicing links sex to neutrophil inflammatory vulnerability
papers.abstract: Mammalian females generally live longer than males, yet the immunological drivers governing sex-biased inflammatory mortality remain unclear. Neutrophils, among conserved immune cells across species, exhibit marked sex differences in inflammatory and age-related diseases. We identified conserved male-biased CD11b expression in resting neutrophils of wild-type mice, Rag2 KO mice, and in human cohorts. Male neutrophils selectively displayed CD11b-dependent transendothelial migration. During tissue inflammation in our mouse model deficient in -Klotho (Kl) combined with Rag2 KO lymphocyte depletion (dKO), males showed higher mortality and more severe pulmonary pathology correlated with increased infiltrating neutrophils in the lung. The neutrophil accumulation directly accounted for heightened IL-1{beta} expression in males despite equivalent per-cell cytokine expression across sexes. Transcriptomic analysis of neutrophils revealed profound sex-biased alternative splicing enriched in Toll-like receptor (TLR) cascades, alongside hormone-responsive regulation of integrin {beta}2 (Itgb2) isoform usage, implicating alternative splicing in neutrophils represents male vulnerability to tissue inflammation.

papers.title: Intravenous BCG Elicits a Sustained Myeloid IFNG Response Signature Associated with Early TB Control
papers.abstract: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) administered intravenously (IV) to rhesus macaques can prevent pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) infection. To establish transcriptional correlates of protection, we generated longitudinal CITE-Seq data across blood and lung after IV BCG in macaques and compared it to clinically approved intradermal (ID) BCG. We define an interferon gamma (IFNG) response signature in alveolar macrophages (AMs) comprising 61 genes with diverging expression between IV and ID BCG from 4 to 16 weeks after vaccination that was also enriched in AMs early after TB challenge. The signature was recapitulated in blood monocytes (IV vs. ID) and associated with protection in an independent cohort of IV BCG-vaccinated macaques. Cell-cell communication analysis inferred increased ligand-receptor interactions in the airway after IV BCG, including those between multiple IFNG-producing T cell subsets and AMs. The sustained IFNG response signature in AMs after IV BCG provides a new correlate and potential mechanism of early TB control informing future vaccine design.

papers.title: Cholesterol and high concentration serum cooperatively enhance canine CAR T cell transduction and expansion
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell immunotherapy is emerging as a promising adjunct treatment option for refractory canine cancers. Unfortunately, clinical trials thus far have failed to meaningfully reduce tumor burden, highlighting the need for improved CAR T cell manufacturing strategies. Effective autologous therapy requires highly viable, efficiently transduced T cells capable of robust expansion, sustained CAR expression, and long-term persistence. Although these parameters have been extensively investigated in humans, comparable optimization in canine systems remains limited. Here, we evaluated culture conditions to improve canine T cell expansion, memory differentiation, and retroviral transduction efficiency. We demonstrated IL-2 supplementation supported superior cellular expansion and preservation of less-differentiated memory phenotypes compared to IL-7 with IL-15. Additionally, we found that increasing cell density during shorter stimulation periods improved expansion while also driving better T cell transduction rates. We discovered that the addition of cholesterol and high-concentration fetal bovine serum (FBS) to media during the transduction period reliably and markedly enhanced transduction efficiency following a single round of retroviral transduction, even at elevated temperatures that would otherwise impair transduction efficiency. This enhancement was observed with both GALV- and RD114-pseudotyped retroviruses and was accompanied by a marked improvement in cellular expansion without driving terminal differentiation of T cell subsets that are prone to exhaustion in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify practical strategies to improve canine CAR T-cell manufacturing and advance the development of clinically viable CAR T cells for canine cancer treatment.

papers.title: Single cell mapping reveals phenotypic, immunometabolic and functional heterogeneity among age-associated B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and aging
papers.abstract: Abstract/Summary Introduction: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) comprise an antigen-experienced memory B-cell population that expands during aging but has also been implicated in autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Cell immunometabolism has emerged as a key determinant of immune-cell function, linking metabolic adaptation to both protective and maladaptive immunity or pathological inflammation, thereby providing a platform for therapeutic intervention. This study aims to comprehensively profile the functional alterations that accommodate ABC expansion, emphasizing metabolic reprogramming within the B-cell compartment in SLE, particularly with regard to ABCs, in order to identify niche metabolic pathways utilized by ABCs that may represent useful therapeutic targets. Methods: An exploratory analysis was conducted using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to phenotypically and functionally characterize ABC populations in patients with SLE and lupus-prone MRL.lpr mice, using a broad array of community tools. We further conducted SCENITH-based metabolic profiling to assess metabolic differences among splenic follicular (FO), marginal zone (MZ) and CD21-CD23- double negative (DN) B cells, in the murine SLE-like MRL.lpr model, in which we tested the ability of B cell subsets to generate protein output, following exposure to specific metabolic inhibitors (2-deoxyglucose and oligomycin). In addition, we cross-examined CD21-CD23- DN B cells in the native context of aging by employing flow cytometry-based analyses of their redox status (NADH/FAD autofluorescence) and mitochondrial function (MitoTracker and TMRE staining) to investigate age-associated metabolic programming. Results: Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed substantial immunophenotypic and metabolic heterogeneity within the ABC compartment in SLE. Subclustering of ABCs revealed three separate and distinct ABC subsets, encompassing CD68 ABCs, NKG7 ABCs, and AREG ABCs, differing in their respecrive transcriptional, functional, and immunometabolic signatures. The CD68 ABC subset demonstrated signs of enhanced cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, lysosomal activity, and increased antigen-processing capabilities. The CD68 and NKG7 ABC populations exhibited increased inflammatory pathway activity, including pattern-recognition receptor signalling and NLRP3 inflammasome-associated activity, while the AREG ABC subset displayed signs of senescence, moderation, exhaustion, or anergy. hdWGCNA identified transcriptional modules associated with acetyltransferase activity, suggesting a potential link between metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodelling through epimetabolite availability, in particular acetyl-CoA. ABCs demonstrated, in general, coordinated amplification of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid utilization, with substantial intragroup metabolic heterogeneity among the three ABC subsets. The CD68 ABCs emerged as the most hypermetabolic subset. In parallel, SCENITH-based metabolic comparison of CD21-CD23- DN B cells between mildly diseased male and severely diseased female MRL.lpr mice revealed increased utilization of alternative non-glucose substrates and enhanced glycolytic activity, but reduced overall protein synthesis capacity, indicating altered allocation of metabolic resources. Further interpretation of the transcriptomic analysis suggests that proteasomal activity could explain the lower protein levels in female MRL.lpr mice, as measured by SCENITH. In addition, in silico drug prediction pointed towards statins and proteasome inhibitors as potentially useful pharmacological agents for blocking cholesterol metabolism and protein degradation, respectively. Finally, the analysis of aged mice also revealed metabolic and redox alterations in ABC-enriched CD21-CD23- DN B cells under physiological aging conditions. Conclusions: Human ABCs appear to comprise a heterogeneous constellation of various subsets possessing different functional properties, as well as different pro-inflammatory or immunoregulatory statuses. ABCs exhibit a distinct hypermetabolic state associated with lupus-related immune dysregulation, but also with aging, in line with previous reports. However, as the disease manifests and progresses, protein production appears to be dampened, which could be attributed to ribosomal problems or proteasome-mediated protein degradation. Metabolic reprogramming is accompanied by enhanced phagocytic and lysosomal programs, which may facilitate the uptake of self-material and contribute to autoreactive immune responses, in particular anti-nuclear autoantibody production. Increased OXPHOS activity may accommodate epigenetic reprogramming towards the atypical memory phenotype displayed by ABCs. Identification of ABC-specific metabolic dependencies may provide opportunities for therapeutic intervention, with lipid consumption being of particular interest. These findings support further investigation of metabolic modulators, including HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and proteasome-targeting strategies, to limit their pathogenic activity in SLE by exploiting their niche metabolic vulnerabilities, in particular their hypermetabolic state and proteostatic stress.

papers.title: Nsg2 deficiency attenuates intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated tumorigenesis through microbiome-dependent metabolic remodeling
papers.abstract: Background & Aims Neuron-Specific Gene 2 (NSG2) is a neuronally expressed protein that facilitates excitatory synaptic transmission through the regulation of AMPA receptor trafficking. While its function has been characterized in the central nervous system, whether NSG2 plays a role in enteric neuronal signaling and intestinal pathology has yet to be explored. We therefore investigated whether Nsg2 deficiency modulates intestinal inflammation and tumorigenesis through gut microbiome-dependent mechanisms. Methods Dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and azoxymethane/DSS-induced colitis-associated cancer (DSS-CAC) models were established in Nsg2-/- and wild-type (WT) mice. Disease severity was evaluated using the disease activity index (DAI), histopathological scoring, and tumor burden assessment. To investigate the potential contribution of the gut microbiota to genotype-associated phenotypes, WT and Nsg2-/- mice were co-housed for six weeks before disease induction. Gut microbial composition and predicted functional pathways were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region) and PICRUSt2, respectively. Results Separately housed Nsg2-/- mice exhibited significantly attenuated DSS-induced colitis, with reduced body weight loss, lower DAI scores, and preserved colonic architecture. In the DSS-CAC model, Nsg2-/- mice developed significantly fewer and smaller tumors with suppressed Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Under co-housing conditions, no statistically significant differences in colitis severity or tumor burden were detected between genotypes, supporting a possible contribution of the gut microbiota to the phenotypes observed in separately housed mice. 16S rRNA sequencing identified distinct microbial communities in Nsg2-/- mice, characterized by greater alpha diversity and enrichment of protective taxa, including Butyricicoccus and Lachnospiraceae. Functional profiling predicted enrichment of methane metabolism, porphyrin biosynthesis, and one-carbon metabolism pathways. Conclusions Nsg2 deficiency confers protection against intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated tumorigenesis, accompanied by alterations in gut microbial composition and suppression of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. These findings identify NSG2 as a novel modulator at the intersection of enteric neuronal signaling, gut microbiota, and mucosal immunity, positioning it as a potential therapeutic target for IBD and inflammation-driven colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Fibronectin binding and non-canonical transcription factor signature distinguishes lung and bone marrow megakaryocytes
papers.abstract: Recent evidence has demonstrated the unique morphology and function of lung megakaryocytes (MKs), yet the source of the differences between lung and bone marrow (BM) MKs remains unclear. While BM MKs are large, polyploid, BM-resident cells primarily known as platelet producing cells, lung MKs are smaller, less polyploid, and known for immunomodulation. To better understand the factors underlying the differences in lung and BM MKs, we developed a flow cytometry method for precise characterization and isolation of MKs using leukocyte exclusion and examination of hematopoietic and canonical MK markers. When MK-leukocyte aggregates are excluded, a single femur+tibia contains approximately 1,493 MKs and a single lung contains approximately 4,541 MKs. Enrichment via positive selection efficiently removes unwanted cells, increasing the percentage of MKs amongst live lung cells by 10.29-fold and the percentage of MKs amongst live BM cells by 29.09-fold. Sorted MKs were viable and spread onto fibrinogen. Gene expression analysis demonstrated that lung MKs increase immune pathway gene expression, including TNFRSF1B. Transcription factor (TF) and cell cycle gene expression decreased in lung MKs compared to BM MKs, including reduced expression of GATA1 and CDC6, possibly explaining observations of low ploidy and size in lung MKs, while expression of the TF ETS2 increased. Lung MKs also express increased ITGA4 compared to BM MKs, abundant surface integrin 4 protein, and increased surface integrin {beta}7 protein compared to BM MKs. Additionally, lung MKs bind significantly more fibronectin ex vivo then BM MKs. These data demonstrate for the first time that lung MKs have a unique TF signature and suggests integrin 4{beta}7 as a relevant receptor for lung MK function.

papers.title: mRNA-1273.262 and mRNA-1283.262 Vaccines Expressing XFG Antigens Neutralize Relevant Circulating Variants
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate and causes substantial disease burden as an endemic respiratory pathogen. Vaccination is a key public health measure to ameliorate the effects of COVID-19 disease but requires annual update to match strains that are circulating. Monitoring of circulating virus and characterization of matched candidate vaccines helps to inform which antigens will provide the greatest benefit to public well-being. The 2026-2027 season will leverage XFG as the variant of interest for vaccine production and in vitro and in vivo data was generated preclinically to support this selection. XFG variant vaccines express well in mRNA format as both full-length spike and linked subdomain antigen formats. Animals immunized with these vaccines elicit robust neutralizing responses to relevant JN.1-family virus variants in both primary series and booster models. In future seasons, robust epidemiologically monitoring including viral genome sequencing will improve early detection of relevant variants and subsequent preparation of vaccine antigens.

papers.title: Transient fetal type 2 bovine viral diarrhea virus infection protects beef cattle from postnatal challenge with type 1b bovine viral diarrhea virus and Mannheimia haemolytica
papers.abstract: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is the most significant disease in feedlot cattle, impacting animal growth, performance, and profitability. Acute bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) infections have been shown to increase the occurrence of BRD. Fetal infection with BVDV during late gestation results in transient fetal infections (TI). At birth, TI calves are negative for BVDV but positive for BVDV-specific antibodies. The objective of this experiment was to determine the effect of TI status on the susceptibility to BRD and the subsequent rate of gain in feedlot cattle. Eight-month-old type 2 BVDV TI and uninfected control heifers (TI-BRD n=5; CON-BRD n=6) were challenged with an intranasal inoculation of non-cytopathogenic (ncp) type 1b BVDV, followed by an intratracheal inoculation with Mannheimia haemolytica. TI and uninfected heifers (TI-CON n=6; CON-CON n=5) were sham-inoculated with media and phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to serve as BRD challenge controls. Heifers were weighed at the beginning and end of the experiment, were evaluated daily for clinical signs of respiratory disease, and jugular blood samples were collected on d 0, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 17, and 31 post-BVDV inoculation. Complete blood count (CBC), flow cytometry, BVDV RTPCR, and serum neutralizing antibody titers for type 1b and type 2 BVDV were measured in blood and serum samples. Average daily gain was similar across treatments. Fetal infection with ncp type 2 BVDV in late gestation resulted in cross-protective immunity, which reduced (P < 0.05) clinical scores, lymphopenia, and viremia in TI heifers following postnatal challenge with a noncytopathic type 1b BVDV and Mannheimia haemolytica compared to challenged control heifers. These findings indicate that fetal BVDV TI may protect offspring from the deleterious effects of combined type 1b BVDV and Mannheimia haemolytica infection during the postnatal period.

papers.title: Recognition of β-D-glucose by surfactant protein D and structural evidence for an extended carbohydrate binding site
papers.abstract: Human surfactant protein D (hSP-D) is an innate immune protein involved in pathogen recognition in the lungs. Structural definition of the recognition of small carbohydrates by rfhSP-D, a biologically and therapeutically active recombinant homotrimeric fragment of hSP-D, has previously revealed the details of calcium dependent binding in the carbohydrate recognition domain and the influence of residues flanking the binding pocket. To provide further structural insight into pathogen exo-polysaccharide recognition by hSP-D and the impact of alternative anomers and linkages, we have used x-ray crystallography and a competitive mannan-based ELISA to investigate the binding of -D-glucose chains (3-7 sugars) and of {beta}-linked glucose trisaccharides derived from long-chain cell wall components of fungal species and allergenic plant components and from extracellular matrices of bacterial biofilms. Our results reveal that a variety of determinants influence the binding configuration, and that SP-D can recognise reducing terminal {beta}-D-glucose through calcium mediated coordination of the O2' and O1' hydroxyls, with the flexibility to recognise alternative epitopes when the preferred target is unavailable for binding. The ligands based on naturally occurring exo-polysaccharides reveal variable, novel and flexible recognition by hSP-D. {beta}-cellotriose and {beta}-laminaritriose exhibit different {beta}-glucose binding modes (non-reducing O3', O4 ' and reducing O1', O2 ' respectively), both with moderate affinity for rfhSP-D. The high affinity {beta}-isomaltotriose ligand binds via the reducing terminal {beta}-glucose O2' and O1' in the calcium-binding pocket, supplemented by interaction of the internal, non-terminal glucose with an extended binding surface, revealing a potential mechanism for high affinity dual-site recognition of extended dextrans.

papers.title: Structural basis of human antibody recognition of linear and conformational epitopes on the peanut allergen Ara h 2
papers.abstract: IgE-mediated food allergy requires allergens to crosslink FcERI-bound IgE on mast cells, yet how individual allergen epitopes organize pathogenic IgE complexes remains poorly understood. We defined the structural basis of antibody recognition of Ara h 2, a major peanut allergen, using three human monoclonal antibodies isolated from IgG1 memory B cells of peanut-allergic children. As IgE, the DPYSPS repeat-specific antibody P4EC10 alone induced degranulation in vitro and passive cutaneous anaphylaxis in vivo, whereas P1BC6 and P1EC5 elicited both responses only when combined. P4EC10 IgG1 inhibited a mean of 46% of Ara h 2 binding to plasma IgE in the highest Ara h 2-specific IgE stratum and 24% in the lowest. Cryo-EM revealed 2:1 and 3:1 P4EC10 Fab-Ara h 2 complexes. In the 2:1 structure, two Fabs bound adjacent linear DPYSPS repeats within the flexible loop and contacted one another. P1BC6 and P1EC5 each bound Ara h 2 with 1:1 stoichiometry and simultaneously engaged distinct conformational epitopes. Solution binding measurements supported these stoichiometries and indicated that proline hydroxylation enhanced P4EC10 binding. These findings show that Ara h 2 can drive effector-cell activation by recruiting a single IgE specificity to repeated epitopes or by engaging distinct IgE specificities at separate conformational epitopes.

papers.title: Mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) fuels iron-sulfur cluster production essential for type I immunity
papers.abstract: Mitochondria orchestrate the metabolic programs that drive T cell-mediated immunity, yet the specific mitochondrial activities that license T cell effector function remain unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) as a critical mitochondrial pathway that supports T cell effector function and limits T cell dysfunction. Upon activation, human and mouse T cells robustly induce mtFAS enzymes in a Myc-dependent manner. Disrupting mtFAS activity in T cells through deletion of the initiating enzyme, malonyl-CoA-acyl carrier protein transacylase (MCAT), sharply reduces effector cytokine production and impairs type I immunity, including CD8+ cytotoxic and CD4+ Th1 responses, to bacterial and viral pathogens in vivo. Loss of MCAT disrupts protein lipoylation and iron-sulfur cluster (ISC) production in T cells, disrupting the stability and function of electron transport chain (ETC) complexes and impairing oxidative phosphorylation. Deletion of ISC biosynthesis machinery phenocopies MCAT loss, whereas selective disruption of protein lipoylation does not. Moreover, selective restoration of protein lipoylation in MCAT-deficient T cells fails to rescue effector function, establishing ISC biogenesis and its downstream support of ETC activity as the principal mtFAS-dependent mechanism sustaining T cell effector function. MCAT deficiency also promotes the premature acquisition of exhaustion-associated features in CD8+ T cells, including increased PD-1 and TIM-3 expression and reduced cytokine competence. Together, these findings establish mtFAS as an essential pathway for initiating and sustaining T cell effector responses, identifying ISC biogenesis and ETC activity as core mtFAS-dependent outputs critical for T cell effector responses and resistance to exhaustion.

papers.title: Extracellular tumor-derived IL-33 promotes ST2-dependent tumor control
papers.abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is a pleiotropic cytokine with both nuclear and extracellular functions as well as context-dependent roles in tumor immunity. Although tumor-derived IL-33 can promote anti-tumor immune responses, the contribution of its subcellular localization and extracellular availability to tumor control remains poorly understood. Here, we generated MC38 mouse adenocarcinoma cells overexpressing distinct IL-33 isoforms to dissect the relative contribution of IL-33 nuclear retention versus extracellular activity in a model of heterotopic tumors. Full length IL-33 (FL), an alanine-mutated isoform (Ala) with impaired chromatin binding and a truncated isoform (Trunc) of IL-33 lacking the nuclear functional domains were stably expressed in MC38 cells. These different IL-33 isoforms exhibited distinct subcellular localization and release profiles but had comparable effects on cell proliferation in vitro. In vivo, IL 33 overexpression reduced tumor growth compared with control MC38 cells, with the most pronounced growth impairment observed in tumors expressing Trunc. Trunc tumors also exhibited the highest levels of extracellular IL-33, which was associated with enhanced IFN-{gamma} production and upregulation of the IL-33 receptor ST2 in tumor-infiltrating T cells. Although CD8+ T cells contributed to tumor control, their depletion did not abolish the differential growth between FL- and Ala-expressing tumors, suggesting that additional cell populations contribute to tumor control. However, genetic ablation of St2 abolished the differential tumor growth associated with the IL-33 isoforms, demonstrating that host ST2 signaling is required for isoform-dependent tumor control. Taken together, our findings identify extracellular cytokine availability as a key determinant of the antitumor activity of tumor-derived IL-33 and support a model in which IL-33 promotes ST2-dependent effector T-cell function. Furthermore, our findings highlight intracellular localization versus extracellular release of IL-33 as potential determinants of the context-dependent effects of the IL-33/ST2 axis in cancer.

papers.title: Single-cell T cell receptor sequencing deciphers αβ- and γδ-T cell responses in neuroblastoma
authors: A. F. W. van der Steeg
papers.abstract: High-risk neuroblastoma is a pediatric tumor with poor survival rates and low MHC-I expression. The cellular determinants of anti-tumor immunity remain poorly defined, limiting development of targeted immunotherapies. We generated a single-cell atlas integrating transcriptomic and {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing of >150,000 T cells from tumor and blood of 10 patients throughout treatment. Fractions of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells are clonally expanded and activated, with tumor-specific expansion among CD4+ cells. Transcriptomic evidence of tumor-reactivity is more pronounced in CD4+ than CD8+ T cells. Moreover, V{delta}1+ {gamma}{delta}T cells are enriched, displaying TCR engagement. Functional screening confirmed reactivity of selected {gamma}{delta}TCRs and, remarkably, a small fraction of CD8+ {beta}TCRs. Subset-specific inhibitory receptors, including CTLA4, FCRL6, and KIRs, may serve as targets for tailored immunotherapies. Together, we identify distinct {beta}- and {gamma}{delta}T cell responses despite low MHC-I, and provide a comprehensive resource for deciphering pediatric immunity against MHC-Ilow tumors.

papers.title: Lipin-1-cardiolipin axis sustains mitochondrial respiration and efferocytosis in macrophages
papers.abstract: Defective macrophage clearance of apoptotic cells contributes to persistent inflammation and cardiometabolic disease. Efferocytosis requires mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, but how macrophages maintain respiratory capacity during resolution remains unclear. Here, we show that lipin-1 supports efferocytosis through a cardiolipin-associated mitochondrial program. In IL-4-stimulated macrophages, lipin-1 deficiency reduced cardiolipin abundance and selectively lowered the abundance of inner mitochondrial membrane proteins, including respiratory-chain components, consistent with decreased mitochondrial respiratory capacity. These defects occurred without broad suppression of canonical metabolic transcriptional programs, and experimentally altering mitochondrial morphology failed to reproduce or rescue the functional phenotype. Disrupting cardiolipin synthesis impaired efferocytosis, whereas the cardiolipin-interacting peptide SS-31 improved mitochondrial respiration and apoptotic-cell clearance in lipin-1-deficient macrophages. Systemic SS-31 treatment also reduced apoptotic-cell accumulation after dexamethasone-induced thymic injury. Together, these findings implicate cardiolipin homeostasis in lipin-1-dependent macrophage bioenergetics and efferocytosis, identifying a potentially actionable pathway while leaving the mechanism connecting lipin-1 to cardiolipin abundance unresolved.

papers.title: Tnfrsf13b Variants Enhance IgG-Mediated Complement Responses to Promote Bacterial Clearance
papers.abstract: RSF13B encodes the TACI receptor, necessary for differentiation of B cells into plasma cells. TNFRSF13B is highly polymorphic, yet common non-synonymous variants including those that impair the receptor structure and/or signaling are retained in the population. Here we show that mice carrying the Tnfrsf13b A144E variant, the murine homolog of the human TNFRSF13B A181E variant associated with common variable immunodeficiency, effectively clear host-adapted Citrobacter rodentium (a murine model of pathogenic E. coli infection) despite nine-fold decreased bacteria-specific IgG compared to WT mice. IgG from Tnfrsf13b mutant mice exhibited reduced sialic acid, terminal galactose, fucose, and showed enhanced complement effector functions, including greater C1q binding and membrane attack complex (C5b) deposition. Results show that some Tnfrsf13b variants enhance complement-dependent antibody effector function, thereby identifying TACI as a regulator of IgG effector properties and providing a potential explanation for the evolutionary persistence of TNFRSF13B mutations.

papers.title: Longitudinal multiomics analysis in blood from individuals before and after HIV acquisition
papers.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of cellular immunity is essential for controlling viral infections, yet individual and coordinated immune responses continue to pose significant challenges in HIV cure research. Recent advances in single-cell and multiomics technologies provide powerful tools to dissect intricate multicellular behaviors and identify novel therapeutic targets. Direct characterization of HIV-induced immune alterations is challenging because matched samples obtained before HIV acquisition are rare. To better understand individual and coordinated cellular immune responses relevant to HIV cure research, we integrated single-nucleus chromatin-accessibility and transcriptomic profiling of 150,060 PBMCs with plasma metabolome, lipidome and soluble immune-profiling from five individuals before HIV acquisition, during early infection and after at least six months of suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART). HIV acquisition expanded activated CD8 T and proliferating NK/CD8 T cells and induced cell-type-specific chromatin and transcriptional changes enriched for interferon, inflammatory and TNF-NF-{kappa}B programs, many persisting during ART. Multiome sequencing detected 32 HIV-positive cells which were associated with increased expression of IFI44L during early infection and ATAD3A after ART. Plasma IP-10 increased transiently, whereas eight energy- or amino-acid-related metabolites showed nominal decreases persisting after ART. These paired observations distinguish transient inflammatory responses from persistent molecular and metabolic perturbations after HIV acquisition.

papers.title: Host glycans trap bacterial lectins to trigger NLRP3 inflammasome activation
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa poses a severe threat to immunocompromised patients through its multifaceted virulence arsenal. Although diverse bacterial components activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, the precise molecular triggers driving this process remain largely elusive. Here, we reveal that host surface glycans effectively trap the P. aeruginosa lectins LecA and LecB, initiating carbohydrate-dependent inflammasome activation. This lectin-mediated cascade exhibits striking host-species and cell-type specificity. The L-fucose-specific LecB activates human blood monocytes and THP-1 cells, where glycosylated {beta}1-integrin contributes to signal transduction, whereas the D-galactose-specific LecA is more potent in murine bone marrow-derived macrophages and dendritic cells. This mechanism requires potassium efflux and displays cell-specific sensitivity to reactive oxygen species. Infection with live bacteria recapitulates the lectin-mediated inflammasome response. Collectively, our findings unveil an unexpected role for host glycans as critical, previously overlooked checkpoints gating P. aeruginosa-driven inflammation, offering fresh insights into host-pathogen dynamics and exposing novel therapeutic targets.

papers.title: MALT1 is an E3 ligase catalyzing its own activation by monoubiquitination
papers.abstract: The protease mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein-1 (MALT1) is an important signaling component of the antigen receptor-induced activation of lymphocytes. Abnormal MALT1 activity is linked to emergence of several lymphoma subtypes. Humans and mice with inactivating MALT1 mutations, on the other hand, show defects in specific classes of immune cells and develop autoimmunity. MALT1 protease activity depends on its inducible K644-monoubiquitination. We have previously identified a negatively charged ubiquitin binding site in MALT1, located ~30[A] from K644, that is necessary for MALT1 monoubiquitination. However, the machinery delivering activated ubiquitin to MALT1 and transferring it to K644 remains unknown. Here we provide evidence that MALT1 is an E3-ligase catalyzing autoubiquitination via a cascade involving MALT1 residue C687, accepting ubiquitin from a ubiquitinated E2-enzyme, and transferring that active ubiquitin to the MALT1 monoubiquitination site, K644. We further identified MALT1 residue Y631, which lies between MALT1(C687) and MALT1(K644), as a gatekeeper of this process. Lymphocyte lines expressing MALT1(C687A) or MALT1(Y631A) mutants showed impaired or increased activation, respectively. Finally, we identified Ube2L3 as a candidate cysteine-specific E2-enzyme servicing MALT1. Overexpression of inactive Ube2L3 compromised MALT1 monoubiquitination and protease activity, indicating Ube2L3 inhibition is a potential means to dampen MALT1 ubiquitination. Collectively, the findings identify MALT1 as an E3 ligase capable of catalyzing its own activation through auto-ubiquitination, which may open new avenues for therapeutic regulation of MALT1 activity.

papers.title: PD-1 inhibition drives CD8 T cell recruitment and T cell-dependent myeloid remodeling in responsive tumors
papers.abstract: While leukocyte recruitment is central to anti-tumor immunity, how recruitment changes over time and following perturbation with immunotherapy is poorly understood because of a lack of tools to identify recruited leukocytes. We used intravenous antibody labeling to characterize recruited leukocytes in murine tumors and evaluated how programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) impacted recruitment. Early PD-1 ICI administration, which induced robust tumor control, increased the density of recently recruited CD8 T cells, and these T cells exhibited a less-exhausted phenotype compared to unlabeled intratumoral CD8 T cells. Early PD-1 ICI also caused a shift in myeloid populations to a proinflammatory iNOS positive phenotype. Delaying PD-1 ICI resulted in ineffective tumor control, which was associated with reduced leukocyte entry per unit volume, less granzyme B upregulation in CD8 T cells, and less iNOS induction in myeloid cells. Use of FTY720 to prevent lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes abolished the protective effects of early PD-1 ICI and reduced CD8 T cell recruitment. While FTY720 did not impact myeloid cell recruitment, it did reduce myeloid iNOS induction. Lastly, PD-1 deletion in CD8 T cells was sufficient to increase CD8 T cell recruitment to tumors and iNOS expression in myeloid cells. These data suggest that CD8 T cell recruitment both increases the quantity and quality of CD8 T cells in the tumor and drives T cell-driven remodeling of the myeloid compartment. These findings support efforts to develop therapies that promote CD8 T cell recruitment to improve immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: An intragastric murine model that recapitulates natural infection with invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella for preclinical evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity and protection.
papers.abstract: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease is a major global health concern, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where young children and immunocompromised individuals are particularly vulnerable. Preclinical models that reproduce the natural course of invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella infection without antibiotic-mediated disruption of the intestinal microbiota are essential for vaccine development. Here, an antibiotic-free murine model is described based on intragastric infection of susceptible C57BL/6 mice with the ST313 clinical isolate Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium D23580. Over seven days, infection progressed from intestinal colonization to extraintestinal dissemination, accompanied by increasing histopathological damage and activation of local and systemic inflammatory responses. The ability of the infection model to evaluate vaccine-induced immunity and protection was assessed by immunizing mice with a formalin-inactivated D23580 strain. Vaccination elicited Salmonella-specific serum IgG and reduced clinical severity, with vaccinated mice showing significantly lower bacterial loads in blood, liver and colon compared with control mice after intragastric challenge. By combining the enteric route, which mimics the natural route of human infection, with an intact intestinal microbiota, this model reproduces key features of progressive invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease and provides a tool for investigating host-pathogen interactions and evaluating vaccine-induced immunity and protection.

papers.title: Intradermal and intranasal vaccination with microparticulated ASFV proteins induces distinct immune profiles in pigs
papers.abstract: African Swine Fever (ASF) is a major threat to the swine industry due to its severe socioeconomic impact and the lack of safe and effective vaccines. Although live attenuated vaccines (LAVs) can induce robust immunity, biosafety concerns restrict their use, making subunit vaccines the preferred alternative. In this context, understanding how vaccination routes modulate immunity is critical. A previous study using a viral vector-based vaccine, encoding for the ASFV antigens p30, p54, p72, p72c and CD2v, induced protection when combining intranasal (IN) and parenteral administrations. However, the relative contribution of each administration route to vaccine-induced immunity remains unclear. Here we investigated how independent and combined vaccination routes influence the immune responses induced by the same ASFV protein cocktail delivered as nanoparticle-based secretory granules. Following a prime-boost regime, pigs vaccinated via intradermal (ID) route seroconverted and developed strong systemic ASFV-specific IgG responses, despite inducing only modest ASFV-specific cellular responses. In contrast, IN administration alone failed to elicit detectable systemic humoral or cellular responses and did not improve the vaccine-induced immunogenicity when combined with the ID route. Following a challenge with a virulent ASFV strain, no protection was achieved in any of the immunized groups. Interestingly, intranasally vaccinated pigs exhibited an accelerated post-challenge ASFV-specific antibody boost in serum compared to controls, suggesting that vaccination through this mucosal route induced immune priming despite the absence of detectable systemic humoral responses before challenge. Overall, these findings reveal distinct route-dependent immune profiles elicited by the same ASFV antigen cocktail and highlight again that robust humoral responses alone are insufficient for protection, further supporting the importance of cellular immunity in vaccine-induced protection.

papers.title: A B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis contributes to myocarditis induced by checkpoint blockade and cardiac irradiation
papers.abstract: Thoracic radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve outcomes in locally advanced lung cancer but can cause cardiac toxicity. The mechanisms by which radiation-associated cardiac injury develops into autoimmune myocarditis during ICI therapy remain incompletely defined. Using autoimmune-prone A/J mice, we investigated whether cardiac irradiation (CIR) promotes a B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis during dual PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade. Dual ICIs plus CIR increased the incidence of myocarditis to 76.2% and cardiac fibrosis to 69.0%. CIR did not further increase global splenic B-cell activation beyond dual ICIs alone but increased cardiac troponin I-reactive B cells and IgG, circulating cardiac autoantibodies (cAAbs), myocardial IgG accumulation, and C3/C3a activation. In mice subsequently found to have grade 3-4 myocarditis on day 21, cAAbs increased by day 7 and continued to rise, preceding histologic identification of severe disease. Cobra venom factor-mediated C3 depletion reduced myocarditis incidence from 90% to 40% and fibrosis from 85% to 35%, while also decreasing B-cell activation and circulating cAAbs. In a separate LLC-OVA tumor model, C3 depletion did not produce an evident loss of the antitumor activity of combined ICIs and radiation under the conditions tested. These findings support a model in which CIR focuses ICI-associated humoral immunity toward cardiac antigens and complement amplifies cardiac injury. The early cAAb rise and protection achieved by C3 depletion provide a rationale for prospective evaluation of cAAbs as a risk marker and complement signaling as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Distinct monocyte replenishment kinetics of macrophages at the oral barrier restrict early-life bacterial colonisation
papers.abstract: Resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) support tissue integrity and homeostasis. However, RTM in the gingiva, the mucosal barrier surrounding the teeth and the site of the prevalent inflammatory disease periodontitis, remain minimally explored. The gingiva experiences a unique combination of challenges, it is continuously exposed to both microbial stimuli and mastication-induced tissue damage; RTM could provide barrier reinforcement against both these challenges. Here we outline that no long-lived macrophage population could be identified within the gingiva. We demonstrate that gingiva macrophages are continuously replenished at a rate not impacted by the considerable microbial burden at this site. Despite microbe-induced signalling failing to determine macrophage replenishment, these signals did play key roles in re-shaping the macrophage network in early-life. We show that microbial-signals drive early-life increases in gingiva macrophages which are transient but vital to restrict the growth of the oral commensal community. Combined, our study delineates the biology of gingiva macrophages across life, outlining a developmentally restricted window during which these cells play key roles in regulating microbial colonisation.

papers.title: DNA Methyltransferase Inhibition During CAR T-cell Manufacturing Enhances Antitumor Activity in Immunocompetent Brain and Ovarian Cancer Models
papers.abstract: Limited persistence and progressive dysfunction remain major barriers to effective CAR T-cell therapy for solid tumors. Epigenetic regulation, particularly DNA methylation, can reinforce dysfunctional T-cell programs by restricting expression of genes required for sustained effector function. CAR T-cell manufacturing provides an opportunity to pharmacologically prime CAR T-cells prior to infusion without additional treatment burden. Therefore, we hypothesized that transient DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) inhibition during CAR T-cell manufacturing would epigenetically modulate CAR T-cell state and enhance functional and antitumor activity against solid tumors. We evaluated transient DNMT inhibition during ex vivo murine CAR T-cell manufacturing using two mechanistically distinct compounds: the nucleoside analogue 5-azacytidine (5-Aza) and the selective DNMT1 inhibitor GSK3685032 (GSK). Epigenetic and transcriptomic profiling, together with functional analyses including repeated antigen stimulation, were performed to characterize the molecular and functional effects of DNMT inhibition on CAR T-cells. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in immunocompetent syngeneic murine models of pediatric glioma and ovarian cancer by assessing tumor burden and survival. 5-Aza treatment induced dose-dependent epigenetic and transcriptional changes in CAR T-cells that were accompanied by enhanced expansion, sustained cytotoxicity and cytokine production during repeated antigen challenge in vitro. These improvements translated in vivo, with enhanced tumor control across immunocompetent models of high-grade glioma, diffuse midline glioma, and ovarian cancer using both B7-H3- and GD2-targeting CAR constructs. The dose associated with the greatest benefit varied by CAR construct and tumor model. In contrast, selective DNMT1 inhibition with GSK did not recapitulate the molecular or functional benefits of 5-Aza and reduced therapeutic efficacy in vivo. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that transient epigenetic modulation during CAR T-cell manufacturing can durably reshape CAR T-cell state and enhance antitumor efficacy. Broad DNMT inhibition with 5-Aza produced molecular, functional, and therapeutic benefits that were distinct from selective DNMT1 inhibition with GSK. These results support transient 5-Aza treatment during manufacturing as a translatable strategy to improve CAR T-cell therapies for solid tumors.

papers.title: Novel Stable 5-OP-RU Analogs Activate Human MAIT Cells and Promote Cytotoxic Antitumor Function
papers.abstract: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are abundant innate-like T lymphocytes that recognize microbial vitamin B2-derived metabolites presented by MR1 and play pivotal roles in infection, autoimmunity, and cancer. Pharmacologic activation with 5-OP-RU, 5-(2 oxopropylideneamino)-D-ribityl-aminouracil potently stimulates MAIT cells and elicits antitumor immune responses, but its intrinsic chemical instability limits therapeutic development. Here, we designed and evaluated novel synthetic 5-OP-RU analogs to improve stability and assess their potential for MAIT directed anti-tumor immunity. Selected analogs induced surface MR1 upregulation and expanded MAIT cells in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy donors and patients with liver cancer. Analog stimulation promoted perforin and granzyme B expression, inflammatory cytokine release, and tumor-cell killing by MAIT-enriched populations in vitro. Structure-activity analysis identified chemical modifications that preserved agonist activity, with several cyclic analogs showing improved chemical and metabolic stability. The series also yielded compounds that upregulated MR1 but inhibited 5-OP-RU-induced MAIT expansion, consistent with antagonist activity. Initial pharmacokinetic studies showed distinct plasma and hepatic exposure profiles in mice. In an orthotopic liver cancer model, select analogs administered with CpG reduced tumor burden and increased hepatic MAIT cell frequency. These findings establish a chemical biology framework for developing stable isolable MAIT ligands as next-generation MAIT-directed cancer immunotherapies.

papers.title: Age- and sex-related variation in TREC and KREC and the association of rs2204985 with TREC in adults
papers.abstract: Background: T-cell receptor excision circles (TREC) and kappa-deleting recombination excision circles (KREC) are indirect markers of new T- and B-cell production. Recorded zero values complicate the analysis of age-related and genetic associations in adult cohorts. Methods: We analyzed 574 adult outpatients aged 39-95 years, including 250 men and 324 women. TREC and KREC were quantified by multiplex real-time PCR and normalized per 100,000 cells. The rs2204985 variant was evaluated using age- and sex-adjusted genetic models. A two-part model separated TREC positivity from quantitative TREC levels among participants with positive values. Alternative regressions and receiver operating characteristic analyses were used for sensitivity and age-classification analyses. Results: Age was more strongly associated with log10(TREC + 0.1) than with log10(KREC + 0.1) (beta = -0.0365 and -0.00728 per year, respectively). Women had higher levels in the main-effects models, although the KREC age association differed by sex. There was no clear evidence of an additive rs2204985 association with TREC positivity (odds ratio = 0.836, p = 0.290). Among the 481 TREC-positive participants, the G allele was associated with higher log10(TREC) (beta = +0.0688 per allele, 95% CI +0.0177 to +0.1199, p = 0.0084; q = 0.0126 across three conditional genetic-model tests). Smearing-corrected marginal predictions for a 58-year-old woman were 40.4 copies/100,000 cells for AA and 53.5 for GG. In the common-positive subset (n = 465), TREC showed higher age-classification AUCs than KREC or their ratio. Conclusions: The rs2204985 association was apparent in conditional TREC levels but not in recorded positivity or full-cohort regression. Analyzing these outcomes separately makes the association easier to interpret, without establishing that zero TREC denotes absent thymopoiesis or that the variant directly alters thymic function.

papers.title: Local macrophage and cDC1 cooperation in the liver drives T-cell immune surveillance against pioneering metastatic cancer cells.
papers.abstract: The liver is one of the most frequent sites for hematogenous metastasis across different types of cancer, but how the liver mounts effective immune responses against arriving tumor cells is not fully understood. Using intravital imaging, we have visualized the initial steps of liver metastasis and delineated three phases in the immune response at the earliest stages of liver metastasis: first, there is continuous surveillance of the liver parenchyma by discrete immune cell subsets in the premetastatic tissue. Second, upon metastatic cell arrival, there is massive neutrophil recruitment and tumor-cell material uptake mediated by resident macrophages. Third, antitumor-specific T-cell activation takes place in situ within intrahepatic leukocyte clusters. We find that tumor-derived material uptake triggers transcriptional programs in liver myeloid cells that upregulate chemoattraction programs in Kupffer cells and cDCs, leading to T-cell activation. Antigen cross-presentation and a functional partnership between cDC1s and local macrophages to recruit and form T-cell activation clusters are required for the elicitation of these intrahepatic T-cell responses. Consequently, prior expansion of cDCs by Flt3L-Ig treatment significantly enhances immunosurveillance, curtailing successful metastasis development. Collectively, our findings identify coordinated immune responses that are essential for anti-metastatic immunity within the liver, uncovering a program to mount defenses against tumor cells arriving in the liver.

papers.title: VisioWell, an all-in-one high-throughput platform to study haematopoietic cells division
papers.abstract: Live-cell imaging has the potential to unravel crucial parameters for haematopoietic normal and leukaemic stem and progenitor cells. Yet, this technology requires a combination of technical and analytical skill sets that can be difficult to find in a traditional haematology lab. We present VisioWell, an all-in-one experimental platform specifically designed to measure the early division dynamics of blood stem and progenitor cells, from a simple brightfield long-term acquisition. We combined a simple custom-made microwell array to trap thousands of individual cells with a powerful semi-automatic analytical pipeline, able to segment, correct, and retrieve the division times for the first three sets of divisions. We validated VisioWell with primary cells from human cord blood and with a cellular model of myeloid leukaemia, revealing that CDK4/6 inhibition induces an increase in asynchronous division. By lowering the technical and analytical barriers to live-cell imaging, VisioWell makes label-free, non-destructive analysis of division dynamics accessible to any haematology lab, while preserving cells for downstream fate and functional readouts.

papers.title: Modular innate recognition in conventional T cells through FcRγ reconstitution
papers.abstract: Engineered T cells can elicit durable tumor responses but largely rely on TCRs or CARs for target recognition. Here we show that FcR{gamma}, an innate signaling adaptor not expressed by conventional T cells, enables full-length innate receptor function in adult human {beta} T cells. FcR{gamma} reconstitution enabled endogenous NKp30 surface expression and cytotoxicity without inducing an innate-like state. Stable co-expression of NKp30 and FcR{gamma} maintained receptor expression after activation withdrawal, supported sustained tumor killing, delayed leukemia progression in mice, and enabled cytotoxicity against primary myeloid leukemia. FcR{gamma} also supported functional import of receptors spanning natural cytotoxicity, Fc receptor, and C-type lectin families, extending conventional T cell responses to tumor ligands, antibody-coated targets, IgE receptor engagement, and microbial patterns. These findings establish a shared-adaptor strategy for expanding innate recognition in engineered T cells while preserving the identity and functional properties of the widely adopted conventional T cell platform.

papers.title: Dynamic T-cell receptor repertoire remodeling is associated with murine and human lung allograft dysfunction
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is a major cause of late graft failure after lung transplantation. Acute cellular rejection is an established risk factor for CLAD. However, its diagnosis by biopsy may incompletely capture dynamic and spatially heterogeneous immune remodeling within the allograft. We investigated whether lung graft proximal T-cell receptor beta-chain (TCR{beta}) repertoire features reflect alloimmune remodeling and associate with acute cellular rejection (ACR) and CLAD. TCR{beta}; sequencing was performed on graft-infiltrating T-cells from a murine orthotopic lung transplant model and on 90 longitudinal bronchoalveolar lavage cell-pellet (BAL-cp) samples from 23 lung transplant recipients during the first post-transplant year. In the murine model, allografts showed persistent histologic injury and strong, consistent TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling relative to isografts. Across days 28 and 56, murine allografts had higher productive clonality (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.0087) and maximum productive frequency (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.014), with complete rank separation at each time point. Murine allografts also exhibited greater pairwise Morisita repertoire overlap (p < 0.0001) and enrichment of recurrent, high-frequency shared clonotypes. Productive clonality from human lung transplant recipients' BAL-cp was higher at the a priori selected month-6 visit from patients who developed CLAD, as compared to those who remained CLAD-free (p = 0.0326). In a month-6 surveillance-visit index analysis, high productive clonality was associated with early onset CLAD (CLAD within 2 years of transplant) (log-rank p = 0.038). In a patient-specific index-event analysis, CLAD-free survival differed across high and low productive clonality groups among acute rejectors (log-rank p = 0.019). Together, these findings establish measurable graft-localized TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling and position BAL TCR{beta}; profiling as a potential complement to biopsy diagnosis. With validation in larger cohorts, graft-proximal repertoire measures may help identify CLAD-associated immune states before the onset of lung function decline and inform more individualized surveillance.
